summary: Admit st-test heavy phases through native resource profiles and retain phase receipts

replay.detail: No replicated claims or projection changes.

schema.detail: No database changes. The local run ledger gains additive admission_receipts entries naming each phase, profile and terminal receipt file.

rules.detail: Member preparation and each heavy check take one native resources exec admission in lane st-test, class check. Independent load, cargo-slot, priority, lane-burst, builds.slice, gate-slot and nice/ionice admission paths are removed. Admission and payload clocks remain separate.

compatibility.detail: Requires native resources exec with --profile, --receipt-file, --request-id, --admission-timeout and --timeout, with the seat endpoint/owner pinned through the JSON CLI, plus owner-scoped resources cancel --request-id --wait with absent-submit tombstones. These flags remain provisional until the native profile contract merges. There is no legacy fallback or ST_EVIDENCE_GOVERN=off bypass. Unsupported hosts refuse heavy phases.

downtime.detail: No daemon restart is performed by this change.

manual.detail: Before adoption, install the native resources CLI/daemon and provision st-test-build and st-test-run host profiles. Proposed seeds for both: cores=4, memory=20615843021 bytes, disk=10000000000 bytes, io=heavy; proposed memory-high=16 GiB. These are declared-provisional full-suite envelopes with client-only learning coverage, not separate measured build/run peaks or measured warm disk growth. Host free-disk floors are separate. The default single member serializes the st-test lane. Receipts persist under ~/.cache/st-test/admission.

recovery.detail: Each request is durably journaled before submission. Cleanup and reuse require one successful whole-tree cancel --wait or a confirmed nonlaunch tombstone. A failed cancellation quarantines scratch, pool tree and shared target; the error prints the request ID, exit code and exact resume command. A later owner attempts cancellation once before reuse and refuses reuse on failure. There are no cancellation retries. Existing signed evidence and terminal receipts are not rewritten.
